question_narrations.en: Final Step 8, What-If-Not Challenge! The final step 8, the proof, is complete! Starting from the 'Checkbox Automation 2019.11.01' starting condition of the imaginary unit i (i's square = -1), which is a new number that becomes -1 when squared, and the complex number a+bi made up of the real numbers a and b, the complex number z = a + bi is clearly divided into the real part (a) and the imaginary part (b), and the sum and product of the complex conjugate number (a - bi), with only the sign of the imaginary part changed, is always a real number. Through algebraic ideas utilizing symmetric structures, it was clearly confirmed that by separating the real and imaginary parts of a complex number and applying the definition of i squared = -1, the conclusion that the 'Checkbox Automation 2019.11.01' property and operation law always holds true. The key point to remember here is that in the complex number a+bi, the imaginary part is not bi, but the real number b multiplied in front of i!
